fig1_rate_by_cohort: Breakage rate by bump class over 2,937 measured release pairs, with Wilson 95% intervals. Counts above each bar are breaking pairs over measured pairs. The y-axis starts at zero.
fig2_rate_by_surface_size: Breakage rate against the size of the exported surface, Wilson 95% intervals, 2,937 measured pairs. The rate moves from 4.1% in the smallest bucket to 40.5% in the largest, so surface size is a confound for any cohort comparison and is reported beside it rather than adjusted away.
fig3_lorenz: Concentration of broken exported symbols. Curves run from the largest contributing pair, so a curve that rises steeply is a cohort whose symbol total belongs to a few pairs. Over all cohorts, 85% of symbols come from the top 10% of breaking pairs (Gini 0.89, 457 pairs). This is why the pair-level rate is the headline and the symbol-level rate is reported with its largest contributor named.
fig4_symbols_per_breaking_pair: Distribution of how much a breaking pair breaks, 457 breaking pairs, log x-axis with doubling bins. The median breaking pair loses 3 exported name(s) and 46% lose two or fewer, while the largest loses 2,941. A mean over this distribution would describe no pair in it.
fig5_unmeasured: Why 780 of 3,777 pairs produced no surface comparison, top eight reasons. Reported because a rate over the measured pairs alone is a rate over a denominator this census chose, and the reasons are not independent of the packages: a package with no importable module is a different exclusion from one whose walk did not finish.
